title: Point-in-time requirements for macroeconomic surprise research
author: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis; Trading Economics

metadata.commercial_dependency: Trading Economics credentials and suitable PIT-history license

chunks.heading: Official-data vintages
chunks.body: ALFRED real-time periods reconstruct which official observations were known on past dates and prevent revised values from leaking into an event study. They do not provide the pre-release economist consensus.

chunks.heading: Consensus and event timing
chunks.body: The documented calendar schema includes UTC release time, actual, previous, revised, consensus forecast and last-update timestamp. Trading Economics also documents point-in-time calendar retrieval, but access and storage remain subject to credentials and subscription rights.

chunks.heading: No proxy consensus
chunks.body: A macro surprise is actual minus the consensus frozen before release. A model forecast, revised actual, current calendar page or vendor forecast is a different variable and cannot silently replace that historical consensus.
